Q2_record_separates: Within the declared numerical generator, estimator-side stopping can be compared with task stopping on identical retained refinement trajectories.
The finite completion-envelope record separates latent pose identity from task-reader invariance: multiple retained pose completions can yield the same task verdict.
The raw-proxy conformal ablation separates high statistical coverage from operational usefulness: a high-coverage set can be too wide to license any ACT.
The learned-shape record separates an observable error-shape model from the subsequent conformal calibration scale; training, calibration, and final evaluation have different roles.
The record separates the nominal conformal coverage target from the realized empirical final-test coverage; 85% observed is not silently rewritten as 90% achieved.
The record separates in-distribution evaluation from a declared 2x sensor-noise stress condition.
The record does not separate numerical-backend behavior from real RGB-D/GPU/robot behavior, and marginal conformal coverage does not establish deterministic safety.

Q4_assumed: Generated asymmetric point clouds are an adequate numerical fixture for testing iterative rigid-registration stopping logic.
Nearest-neighbour point-to-point ICP with damped Kabsch updates is a useful iterative pose-refinement proxy.
The local linearized dispersion, proposed update, RMS residual, and normalized stage are useful observable features for a simple error-shape model in this numerical generator.
The six log-linear shape regressions are treated as frozen after TRAIN; they are not claimed to be optimal or transferable to a real pose estimator.
TRAIN, CALIBRATION, and FINAL TEST episodes are exchangeable only within the declared in-distribution numerical generator; the 2x-noise stress condition intentionally violates that match.
The fixed numerical floors are regularizers selected for this fixture, not physical constants.

Episode-level split-conformal calibration licenses a marginal coverage interpretation only under its statistical assumptions; it is not a deterministic safety certificate or conditional guarantee for every context.
The completion set is a retained computational construction of still-admissible alternatives, not a claim that every member exists or that a numerical set describes the full physical world.
The current robust box/L1 task readers are exact only for the declared monotone numerical predicates; no such reader validity is claimed for arbitrary physical manipulation.
Wall-clock timing is machine-specific and secondary to iteration counts and independently evaluated numerical task outcomes.
